note: Canonical HTTP path vectors (plans: coverage wave 1, design §1.1). Every frontend and the core must map `in` to `out` exactly. A hole the frontend could not resolve is written into the input as the two characters {} before canonicalising.
rules: 1. If the input starts with a scheme (case-insensitive http:// or https://) or with //, drop the scheme and the authority up to the next /; nothing left means /.

4. Per segment, first match wins: `{$}` -> dropped; `{*}` -> {*}; `*` or a segment starting with `*` -> {*}; `{name...}` -> {*}; `[...x]` or `[[...x]]` -> {*}; contains { or [ , or starts with : -> {}; else the literal, case preserved.
5. Everything after the first {*} is dropped.
6. Result is / followed by the segments joined by /, or / when there are none.
